== Current conclusion ==

'''Alan Glasgw''' is known from a printed abstract of business at the Jedburgh justice ayre on 26 February 1495. The entry records the slaughter of Alan Glasgw among offences covered by a remission produced by James Pilmure, described as ''in Ednem''. It does not identify Alan's residence, occupation, parents, spouse, heirs, place of death or exact date of death.<ref name="Alan1495">Robert Pitcairn, ed., ''Criminal Trials in Scotland, from A.D. M.CCCC.LXXXVIII to A.D. M.DC.XXIV'', vol. I, part I (Edinburgh, 1833), p. 19. Pitcairn's printed “1594–5” is a typographical error for 1494–5; the entry belongs to the second day of the Jedburgh ayre, 26 February 1495. Pilmure is described as ''in Ednem'', not “of Ednam”.</ref>

Because Alan belongs before 1500, this free-space page—not a new WikiTree person profile—is the appropriate place for his documentary evidence.

== Record and interpretation ==

James Pilmure produced a remission that included the slaughter of Alan Glasgw. Ralph Ker became surety that Pilmure would satisfy the injured parties.<ref name="Alan1495" /> The Alan item is separate from the preceding case involving George Smythe and should not be combined with it.

The underlying contemporary court book is National Records of Scotland reference '''JC1/1'''.<ref name="JC11">National Records of Scotland, JC1/1, Court Books, old series, South Circuit and Edinburgh, 7 November 1493–13 August 1504.</ref> Published research places nearby Jedburgh business at folios 27v–28r, but Alan's exact folio has not yet been established.<ref name="Armstrong2013">Jackson W. Armstrong, “The Justice Ayre in the Border Sheriffdoms, 1493–1498”, ''Scottish Historical Review'', vol. 92, no. 1 (2013), pp. 1–37, including references to NRS JC1/1, fols. 27v–28r; doi:10.3366/shr.2013.0136.</ref>

NLS Adv. MS. 6.1.4 is a circa-1809 transcript of the court material, not a contemporary transcript.<ref name="NLSAdv614">National Library of Scotland, Adv. MS. 6.1.4, transcript, circa 1809, of Scottish justiciary court records covering November 1493–August 1504.</ref> The original JC1/1 entry should be inspected before the printed absence of ''de'' is treated as conclusive manuscript evidence.

== What is not proved ==

No inspected source connects Alan to an earlier or later Glasgow bearer. The record does not prove a hereditary surname, a Borders residence, or any family relationship.
